Car: A description of the class Car, characterized by its sleek and aerodynamic design with body panels made from lightweight materials such as aluminum or carbon fiber, and equipped with advanced lighting systems that include LED headlights and taillights. Behavioral traits or functional features include a powerful hybrid engine capable of achieving high speeds while maintaining fuel efficiency, automated driving capabilities allowing for hands-free operation on highways, and a sophisticated infotainment system with voice commands and connectivity options for seamless navigation and entertainment.
Ped: A description of the class pedestrian, characterized by their agility and ability to navigate through urban environments with ease, and equipped with the functional features necessary for crossing roads safely, such as looking both ways before proceeding.
vehicle: A description of the class vehicle, characterized by sleek aerodynamic designs and advanced safety systems, equipped with high-performance engines and state-of-the-art connectivity features, enabling seamless navigation and entertainment experiences.
vulnerable_road_user: A description of the class vulnerable road user (pedestrians and cyclists), characterized by their mobility and susceptibility to traffic risks, and exhibiting behaviors that prioritize safety and navigating through complex urban environments.
Cyc: A description of the class cyclist, characterized by their slender build, often adorned with reflective clothing at dusk and dawn, and equipped with a helmet to protect against potential collisions. Cyclists exhibit a high level of caution and awareness on the road, maintaining a steady pace while scanning their surroundings constantly. They frequently use hand signals to indicate turns and stops, making themselves visible to drivers and other cyclists. When crossing intersections, they pause to ensure safety, preferring to follow traffic lights rather than risking unpredictable vehicular movements. Cyclists also display a sense of community, often sharing lanes with pedestrians and other cyclists, and they respect others' space and right of way, even when they are at a disadvantage due to their slower speed.
